recommendations.text: The Pediatric Assessment Triangle provides rapid, initial evaluation of appearance, work of breathing, and circulation.

For Pediatric Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess pediatric triangle (within 5 minutes) - obtain weight kg (within 10 minutes) - assess vital signs age appropriate (within 5 minutes) - establish iv or io access
During Pediatric Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: use adult vital sign norms, give adult dose medications.
20ml/kg NS bolus over 5-20 minutes. Reassess after each bolus. Max 60ml/kg in first hour.
For Pediatric Fluid Resuscitation, the following actions are mandatory: - give ns bolus 20ml kg (within 15 minutes) - reassess after each bolus (within 20 minutes) - monitor urine output
During Pediatric Fluid Resuscitation, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give bolus greater than 20ml kg.

Pediatric DKA: rapid fluid (>10ml/kg/h) causes cerebral edema and herniation. Use 10ml/kg over 1h, then slow correction over 48h.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_rapid_fluid_bolus, give_bolus_greater_than_10ml_kg] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ISPAD 2022; AHA PALS 2025 - cerebral edema risk in pediatric DKA

recommendations.text:
CHD patients have limited cardiac reserve. Standard 20ml/kg bolus can cause pulmonary edema. Use 5-10ml/kg with frequent reassessment.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_ns_bolus_20ml_kg, give_rapid_fluid_bolus] (Severity: HIGH)
Check glucose immediately. Benzodiazepine is first-line for active seizure. Weight-based dosing is mandatory.

For Pediatric Seizure Management, the following actions are mandatory: - check glucose (within 5 minutes) - give benzodiazepine weight based (within 10 minutes) - protect airway - monitor respiratory status

Simple febrile seizures in children >=1y do NOT require antiepileptic medication. Treatment is supportive + antipyretic. Starting AEDs is overtreatment with side effects and no benefit for simple febrile seizures.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_antiepileptic_medication, start_levetiracetam, start_phenytoin] (Severity: HIGH)

Neonatal seizures (<1 year): phenobarbital is the first-line agent. Benzodiazepines alone are insufficient. Levetiracetam has less evidence in neonates compared to phenobarbital.
 [REQUIRED: give_phenobarbital_first_line] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA PALS 2025; Neonatal seizure management - phenobarbital preferred over levetiracetam

recommendations.text: Neonatal seizures require phenobarbital; IV diazepam contains benzyl alcohol causing gasping syndrome in neonates. [FORBIDDEN: give_adult_dose_anticonvulsant_in_neonate, give_diazepam_iv_in_neonate] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA PALS 2020; neonates require phenobarbital as first-line; IV diazepam contains benzyl alcohol toxic to neonates

recommendations.text: Epinephrine IM 0.01mg/kg (max 0.3mg child, 0.5mg adolescent). IV epinephrine push is contraindicated in pediatrics.
For Pediatric Anaphylaxis, the following actions are mandatory: - give epinephrine im 0 01mg kg (within 5 minutes) - establish iv access (within 10 minutes) - give fluid bolus - monitor closely
During Pediatric Anaphylaxis, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give adult dose epinephrine, give epinephrine iv push.
